title: Location Data Disclosure
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) at regular intervals. This action causes the threat because the device shares sensitive location data with an external system.
assumptions: The device is capable of transmitting GPS data and the backend is capable of receiving and storing it.

title: Location Data Transmission
description: The data flow (DF1) transmits live GPS coordinates from the device to the backend. This data-centric threat arises because the transmission of location data (meta-data) can be used to link or identify the parties involved.
assumptions: The device and backend are identifiable by the GPS coordinates being transmitted.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The backend (P1) receives and processes the transmitted GPS coordinates. This action causes the threat because the backend stores or processes location data, which may be used for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The backend is capable of storing and processing the received GPS data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 writes location pings to DataStore DS1. This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data (location pings) to a third-party data store, which may be considered a known or unknown third party depending on the store's nature. The minimality principle is key: only strictly required personal data should be disclosed.
assumptions: The location pings contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the data store is considered a 'known third party' under the specific LINDDUN Pro definition of data disclosure, as the store's identity and data retention policies are not fully specified in the context.

title: Linking Threat
description: Data in transit (DF2) carries metadata about the parties involved (Process P1 and DataStore DS1). This metadata could be used to link or identify the data subjects, creating a privacy risk during transmission.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata that could be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: Assumes standard data-centric threats apply to the transmission of process and data identifiers.

title: Data Disclosure
description: DataStore DS1 receives the location pings from Process P1. The store's processing or storage of this data may cause a threat if it retains or processes the data in a way that exposes personal information, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: The data store's storage practices are not fully specified in the context.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the store's storage practices constitute a 'threat' under LINDDUN Pro, as the context does not specify the store's data handling policies.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (P1) shares personal location data with the backend (P1) for processing, which constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred to a known third party (the backend) for processing.

title: Linking
description: The data flow (DF3) transmits location pings to the backend, potentially allowing the backend to link or identify the user via meta-data about the parties being used to link them.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The geofencing engine (P2) receives the location pings and processes them to check zone entry/exit, which involves processing personal data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) shares configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) with the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). If DS2 is not properly secured or if the zone definitions are not encrypted, an unauthorized party could access this data and potentially use it to identify or track individuals.
assumptions: DS2 is accessible to external entities without proper authentication.

title: Data-Linking Threat via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF4) transmits zone definition metadata (e.g., 'home', 'school', 'friend's house') to the Geofencing Engine (P2). This meta-data could be used to link or identify the parties involved in the data flow, potentially compromising privacy if the metadata is not sufficiently obfuscated.
assumptions: The zone definitions contain identifying information about the individuals.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Geofencing Data
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives the zone definitions and processes them to determine if a user is in a configured zone. If P2 is not properly secured or if the processing logic is flawed, an unauthorized party could access the processed results and potentially use them to identify or track individuals.
assumptions: P2 is accessible to external entities without proper authentication.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Process (P2) shares arrival/departure notification data with the ExternalEntity (EE1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This allows EE1 to potentially access sensitive location data for unauthorized purposes.
assumptions: No authentication or authorization mechanism is in place between P2 and EE1.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits arrival/departure notification data. The threat arises from the meta-data associated with the data flow, which may contain information about the parties involved (e.g., P2 and EE1) that could be used to link or identify them, even if the data itself is not sensitive.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata that could be exploited for identification.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Location Data
description: The ExternalEntity (EE1) receives the arrival/departure notification data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. For example, EE1 may store the location data without proper consent or in a way that allows for future unauthorized access or profiling.
assumptions: EE1 stores the data in a manner that enables future unauthorized access or profiling.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its identity (name, DOB, school) with the Mobile App Backend (P1) to create the child's profile. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the source element where the act of sharing causes the exposure of sensitive personal data.

title: Data Processing/Storage
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) receives the parent's identity data and stores it in a way that causes a threat. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the destination element where the recipient processes or stores the data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Mobile App Backend) shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with DataStore DS2. This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.
assumptions: The data is considered strictly required for the application's functionality.
uncertainty_note: Assumption made that the data is strictly required; if additional data is needed for processing, this may be an implicit disclosure.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Data-centric threat: The data flow DF7 carries personal data (account, child profile, geofence zone) across the network. This data may be used to link or identify the parties involved in the flow.
assumptions: No specific meta-data about the parties is known or used.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if any meta-data about the parties is used to link or identify them during transit.

title: Data Disclosure
description: DataStore DS2 receives the data from Process P1 and stores it. The act of storing this data may cause a threat if the stored data is used to identify or link parties in ways not intended by the system.
assumptions: The data is stored as-is without additional processing that could reveal sensitive information.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the stored data is used to identify or link parties.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its current location or location history with the Mobile App Backend (P1) without explicit consent or a data-sharing agreement.
assumptions: Parent assumes the Mobile App Backend will not misuse the location data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend has a formal policy to restrict location data sharing.

title: Location Data Transmission
description: Location data is transmitted over the network (data in transit) between EE1 and P1, potentially exposing the data to interception or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Network security measures are in place to protect the data.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard encryption is used for the data transmission.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) processes the location data in a way that causes a privacy threat, such as storing it for future use without the parent's consent.
assumptions: Backend processes location data for map display purposes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend has a formal policy to restrict location data storage.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The data store (DS1) is accessible to the mobile app backend (P1) without explicit authorization controls. This allows P1 to retrieve sensitive location history data, which may be used to identify or track the parent entity.
assumptions: The system allows direct access from DS1 to P1 without authentication or audit logging.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits location history data to P1. The metadata associated with this flow (e.g., timestamps, data types, source identifiers) may be used to link or identify the parent entity and its associated data.
assumptions: The data flow metadata is not encrypted or obfuscated to prevent correlation.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the location history data and processes it to serve a map/history view. This processing may involve storing, aggregating, or displaying the data in a way that compromises privacy.
assumptions: The backend does not have appropriate access controls or data minimization policies in place.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity (e.g., name, contact info, or other identifying attributes) with the mobile app backend (P1) to facilitate the invitation process. This action causes a privacy threat because the recipient (P1) may use this information to link or identify the parent, potentially violating the parent's privacy rights.
assumptions: The parent entity has a modeled identity that can be exposed during the interaction.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow (DF10) transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., the parent's identity and the mobile app's identity) in transit. This data-centric threat arises because the mobile app backend (P1) may use this meta-data to link the parent to the app, potentially enabling the app to identify or track the parent.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination element (P1) receives the parent's identity and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. The mobile app backend may use this data to link the parent to the app, potentially enabling the app to identify or track the parent.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores the parent's identity in a way that causes a privacy threat.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The backend process (P1) grants access to the secondary guardian (EE3), which is an external entity. This interaction is invalid per the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity is not a valid interaction type), meaning the backend does not have a modeled flow to share data with an external entity. Consequently, the act of sharing data with an external entity is not a valid privacy threat in this context.
assumptions: The backend process (P1) is a valid process, and the secondary guardian (EE3) is an external entity.
uncertainty_note: The mapping table explicitly excludes 'Process->ExternalEntity' as a valid interaction. Therefore, the threat of unauthorized access to an external entity is not applicable here.

title: Data-centric Threat
description: The data flow (DF11) transmits live location data from the backend (P1) to the secondary guardian (EE3). This data-centric threat arises from the transmission of sensitive personal data (live location) over the network. The act of sharing this data with an external entity (EE3) creates a risk of the data being intercepted, logged, or used to identify the user.
assumptions: The data flow (DF11) exists and transmits live location data.
uncertainty_note: The threat of data-centric threats (meta-data about parties) is a standard LINDDUN Pro concern for any data flow involving external entities.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The secondary guardian (EE3), as the destination element, receives the live location data. As an external entity, it may process or store this data in ways that cause threats, such as retaining it for future use, sharing it with other parties, or using it for profiling. The act of receiving and processing data from an external source creates a privacy risk.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is an external entity that receives and processes the data.
uncertainty_note: The threat of unauthorized processing by the destination element is a standard LINDDUN Pro concern.

title: Unauthorized Access to Aggregated Data
description: The process P1 shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an external entity (EE4). If the partner lacks appropriate access controls or if the data is not encrypted, an unauthorized party could access this sensitive information.
assumptions: The partner does not have explicit, granular access controls for this specific data set.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the partner has implemented the necessary security measures to prevent unauthorized access.

title: Data-Linking Threat via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF12 transmits usage and engagement analytics. If the partner's metadata (e.g., IP addresses, device IDs, or user identifiers) is exposed during transit, it could be used to link or identify the data subjects, even if the data itself is not directly visible.
assumptions: The partner's metadata collection or transmission practices are not fully secured.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the partner's metadata practices are fully secured.

title: Unauthorized Processing or Storage
description: Upon receiving the analytics data, the external entity (EE4) may process or store it in a way that causes privacy threats, such as re-identifying users or storing it in a way that is not compliant with privacy regulations.
assumptions: The partner's internal processing or storage practices are not fully compliant with privacy regulations.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the partner's internal processing or storage practices are fully compliant with privacy regulations.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity EE2) sends a manual check-in/SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process P1). This action attributes the data (the message and its associated location data) to the user, creating a potential non-repudiation risk where the parent cannot deny the message's existence or content.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and stored by the parent.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The parent (Process P1) receives the SOS message and stores it. Processing this data for a manual check-in/SOS may involve storing the message in a database or log, which could be a source of privacy threats if the data is accessed or used without proper authorization.
assumptions: The parent processes the message as intended.
